Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, patchy airspace opacities (consolidations) in the mid-to-lower lung zones with visible air bronchograms and no significant lymphadenopathy or cavitation. This radiological pattern of persistent, non-segmental consolidation is a classic presentation for low-grade B-cell lymphoma of bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue (BALT lymphoma), which often mimics pneumonia but fails to resolve with antibiotics.
